Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild brings up a general question about navigating a new phase of their life.
Situation2: This is the last weekend before the partner relocates abroad for months.
Story: I sat at the kitchen table, my phone buzzing with a message from my partner: “Can’t wait for our weekend together. Just us.” My heart fluttered, knowing this was our last chance to be close before she left for months. I’d promised her my undivided attention, a weekend of memories to hold onto. Just then, my grandson wandered in, his eyes uncertain. “Grandpa, can I talk to you?” he asked, voice small. He was on the brink of adulthood, facing choices I remembered all too well. He wanted my advice, my stories, my time—he needed me to be the wise, steady presence I’d always tried to be. I glanced at the clock, feeling the weight of both worlds pressing in. My partner’s suitcase was already by the door, her expectations clear. My grandson’s hopeful gaze tugged at me, too. I felt torn, my heart pulled in two directions, each demanding a part of me I wasn’t sure I could give.
